analysis.title: October CPI Preview And How To Trade It: A Shutdown Ghost, A Health Insurance Cliff, And The Print That Decides December
key_insights: October CPI (Tuesday Nov 10, 8:30am ET) has no year-over-year headline or core print because the BLS never collected October 2025 prices during last year's government shutdown. The market trades core CPI month-over-month.
Consensus expects headline CPI +0.3% M/M (September was +0.6%) and core +0.2% M/M (unrounded consensus mean 0.22%, September was 0.33%). Gasoline was more than half of September's headline increase.
Goldman is the low forecast at 0.16% core M/M. JPMorgan's Mike Feroli is the high at 0.23% core (headline 0.25%). Deutsche Bank is at 0.20% on both headline and core.

Goldman expects core to roughly halve from September's pace on three components: airfares flat (after +2.5% per month on average this year), health insurance -2.5%, and autos weak (used cars -1.5%, new cars +0.1%, auto insurance -0.3%).

Health insurance is the biggest drag. The BLS applies its semiannual update of insurer source data in October. Goldman expects meaningfully negative readings for six months until the April reset, pushing medical care services (9% of core) to -0.1%.

Goldman estimates that the BLS interpolation of the missing October 2025 data (geometric mean of September and November) leaves residual seasonality that boosts October seasonally-adjusted core CPI by 5bp. Excluding it, Goldman's underlying core is about 0.11%, which is also its estimate for November and December.
Goldman sees shelter payback: OER slows to 0.26% from 0.35%, rent to 0.23% from 0.25%, hotels to 0.5% from 2.0%.

Deutsche Bank (Brett Ryan, Matt Luzzetti) sees similar shelter and health insurance dynamics but more strength in recreation and information technology commodities and in recreation services (streaming prices), ending 4bp above Goldman.

Goldman's CPI forecast maps to a larger 0.23% core PCE, because used cars weigh less in PCE and the PCE source data for health insurance, auto insurance and airfares should show increases. Deutsche is at 0.20% core PCE, keeping the annual rate near 3.1%.

Fed context: the FOMC held at 3.75%-4.00% on Oct 28 in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike. Payrolls rose 165K versus a 70K estimate, with 84K upward revisions and unemployment at 4.1%. A December hike is about 86% priced (21.4bps of 25, per Goldman rates as of Monday's close). The Dec 9 meeting is described as turning on inflation.
Goldman rates strategists call a strong labor market a prerequisite for further hikes but not a determinant.

Goldman STIR trading prefers H7H8 flatteners, since a consensus-or-hotter core takes December to a full hike. Swaps trading has been cutting longs and its steepening bias and is paying 5s10s30s and flattening 5y2y/7y3y. The Treasury desk thinks dips are more likely bought than rallies sold given light long positioning.

JPMorgan's Jay Barry sees front-end yields reversing higher and is putting on 5s/10s breakeven steepeners, opposite to Goldman strategists, who still want to own 5s on the 2s5s30s fly and like TIPS on a beta-weighted basis.
Treasury sells $42B of 10-year notes at 1pm ET after the print, part of a $125B refunding. The 10Y yield is at 4.87%.

Goldman FX trading took back half of its EURUSD cash short after NFP and will likely reduce further into CPI. Key levels are 1.1210/15 on the topside and 1.1105/20 on the downside. Most dollar pairs price a 25-35bp spot move.

Monday's S&P rally of +2.35% to 7,550 (best day in over seven months, VIX down almost 6 vols to 19.92) left the index at the CTA medium-term trigger of 7,548. Goldman's desk estimates CTAs are sellers in every scenario this week. Its favored expression is IWM upside into month-end (27-Nov 290 calls).

Options market: Tuesday's S&P straddle is 80bps (about $60), up from 52bps last month. Through Friday's PPI it is 1.49%. Monday's straddle realized almost 2x. JPMorgan expects PPI +0.6% headline and +0.4% core.

The author argues a soft core print buys a relief rally that Friday's PPI could reverse, while a firm print locks in December with CTAs already selling. A consensus print gives the BLS seasonals as an excuse.
Goldman's risk is to the upside if oil disruptions return. WTI is at $87 on Trump calling further Iran strikes highly unlikely.

trade_ideas.rationale: Steepening in whites/reds is attributed mainly to positioning and stops in macro expressions like 2s10s, and flatteners offer favorable risk/reward if risk wobbles again.
trade_ideas.risk: A soft core CPI would reduce December hike pricing and hurt the flatteners.

risk_factors: Oil disruptions returning would put inflation risk to the upside, per Goldman. WTI is at $87.
A soft CPI driven by health insurance (a methodology reset that does not touch PCE) and used cars (small weight in PCE) may be discounted by the Fed.
Household inflation expectations are near a three-year high, and PPI is running well ahead of CPI.
CTAs are sellers in every scenario this week, with the S&P at the 7,548 trigger.
The 1pm 10-year auction ($42B) could add rate volatility. A hot print means a concession.
Seasonal distortion from the shutdown interpolation may add about 5bp to October core CPI and make the print harder to interpret.
Goldman admitted last month that AI blew up its inflation forecast, which weakens confidence in its low estimates.
vol_and_positioning: Tuesday's S&P CPI-day straddle is 80bps (about $60), up about half from last month's 52bps, the cheapest CPI straddle of the year. The straddle through Friday's PPI is 1.49%. Monday's straddle realized almost 2x.
VIX fell almost 6 vols to 19.92 on Monday after a +2.35% S&P rally to 7,550.
The S&P sits at the CTA medium-term trigger of 7,548. Goldman's desk estimates CTAs are sellers in every scenario this week.
IWM upside into month-end (27-Nov 290 calls) is Goldman's favored expression, on strong seasonals, low positioning, a high short base and the cheapest vol on the board.
Most dollar pairs price a 25-35bp spot move for CPI, below recent averages.
Treasury desk sees light long positioning, so dips are more likely bought than rallies sold.
geopolitical: Trump calls further Iran strikes highly unlikely, which keeps WTI at $87. Goldman flags upside inflation risk if oil disruptions return.
The 2025 US government shutdown left no October 2025 CPI data, which removes the year-over-year comparison and distorts the seasonal factors.
Midterm elections the prior week produced a 'Blue Tsunami' result, with the S&P's fourth straight weekly loss of -2.7%.
cross_bank_references: Goldman is the clear dove at 0.16% core, JPMorgan's Feroli is the hawk at 0.23%, and Deutsche sits in the middle at 0.20%.
JPMorgan's Jay Barry is on the other side of Goldman's front-end view, expecting front-end yields to reverse higher.
Deutsche Bank's Brett Ryan and Matt Luzzetti land in a similar place to Goldman on shelter and health insurance but find more heat elsewhere, ending four hundredths above Goldman.
There is no JPMorgan scenario matrix available at the time of writing.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's 0.16% core forecast and 0.1% path for November and December would make the September hike look like one-and-done, based on health insurance, autos and shelter payback.
tension_points.bear_case: The components carrying the miss are a health insurance methodology reset that does not touch PCE and used cars with a small PCE weight. Inflation expectations are near a three-year high, PPI is running ahead of CPI, and a consensus-or-hotter core locks in a December hike with CTAs already selling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core CPI print of 0.25% or higher would send December to a full hike and bring January into play.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman STIR trading expects H7H8 flatteners to perform as the December FOMC moves toward a full hike, and Goldman Treasury sees dips bought given light long positioning.
tension_points.bear_case: JPMorgan's Jay Barry expects front-end yields to reverse higher and is putting on 5s/10s breakeven steepeners.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core CPI print at or below 0.16% would cut December pricing and hurt H7H8 flatteners.
